issues.detail: The Greek 'παρακαλω' (parakallō) is a verb meaning 'I urge/exhort/beseech', but the Vietnamese 'khuyên' (advise/urge) combined with 'con' (child/son) changes the relationship. The Greek does not contain a word for 'child' or 'son'. More importantly, 'παρακαλω' is 1st person singular ('I'), and while the Vietnamese captures the 'I', it adds a familial hierarchy ('con') not present in the text.
The Greek 'μαλλον' (mallon) meaning 'rather' or 'more so' is omitted in the Vietnamese translation.
